newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- new deals steal stage.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- new deals steal stage.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond secondary prices were modestly higher at midday, but a bustling primary market--including a $468 million New York City general obligation bond offering--was commanding the focus.
JP Morgan Securities Inc tentatively priced the city's GOs at top yield of 5.575 in 2022.
The yield was slightly higher than the 5.55 percent maximum yield offered to individual investors during the deal's retail order period.
One trader said the offering appeared to be going "pretty well."

"I think this is a bit of an odd situation," he said. "First of all it's very rich, but despite the fact that it's rich, I believe that (JP) Morgan and perhaps the others are going to stand up for the deal," the trader said. "I think they are trying to make an impression."

Now is as a good a time as any for impression making, he said. Spreads on city paper have tightened by 25 to 30 basis points over the course of last four or five deals, and little other paper is around to compete with the city's deal, he said.
"You know a third of the deal is done, they'll get enough of it distributed, and they'll take down the rest of it," the trader said. "That's my suspicion."

Also Tuesday, Goldman Sachs & Co won $39.2 million New York City fixed-rated taxable GOs. The offering featured a top yield of 6.58 percent in 2001, a 47 basis point spread over comparable U.S. Treasuries.

Meanwhile in London Tuesday, Goldman Sachs & Co priced $75 million New York City floating rate Euronotes, 24 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate, a city official said. The offering marks the City's third such sale. Its last sale was done at 28 basis points over LIBOR, he said.

As for the municipal secondary market, one trader judged it up 1/8 to 1/4 point coming off Monday's softness. A second trader described secondary prices as a few basis points stronger, but taking a backseat to new issues.
"That's really where the focus is," he said.
On the competitive side, Orange County, Fla., Nassau County, N.Y., and Illinois contributed sizeable deals Tuesday.
Lehman Brothers Inc said it won $217 million Orange County tourist development tax refunding revenue bonds at a true interest cost of 5.266 percent.
First Albany Corp said it won $191 million Nassau County serial government improvement bonds at a net interest cost of 4.737 percent.
First Chicago Capital Markets said it won $100 million Illinois GOs at a true interest cost of 5.10 percent.

On the negotiated side, Smith Barney Inc repriced Alegent Health - Immanuel Medical Center, Nebraska's $58 million bond deal, lowering yields in several maturities. The offering featured a top yield of 5.425 percent in 2021.
Elsewhere, AG Edwards & Sons Inc tentatively priced $33.4 million Grandville Schools, Mich., refunding bonds at a top yield of 5.31 percent in 2015.
George K Baum & Co tentatively priced $32 million Colorado Regional Transportation District bonds at a top yield of 5.05 percent in 2012.
CoreStates Capital Markets tentatively priced $30 million Exeter Township, Berks County, Pa., general obligation bonds at a top yield of 5.40 percent in 2021.

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was up 11/32 at 101-14/32 to yield 6.51 percent. A wave of foreign buying lifted the market ahead of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's scheduled Humphrey Hawkins testimony before a House of Representatives banking committee at 1400 EDT.
In debt futures, the September municipal contract was up 9/32 at 120-12/32. The September T-bond contract was up 9/32 at 114-9/32. The MOB spread was 195 ticks.
--Kathie O'Donnell, 212-859-1655
